column1: DENGUE CASE REPORTING During the 36th week, 1153 suspected dengue cases were reported across 22 districts, compared to 1295 cases in the    previous  week,  reflecting  11%  decrease.  The  Western Province  accounted  for  44.9%  of  total  cases,  with  the Colombo  Municipal  Council  (CMC)  contributing  2.9%, the  rest  of  Colombo  District  16.4%,  Gampaha  District 19.4%,  and  Kalutara  District  6.2%.  Outside  the  Western Province,  notable  case  contributions  were  reported  from Kandy  (13.8%),  Kegalle  (5%),  Ratnapura  (4.8%),  Galle (4.1%),  Matara (3.6%), Puttalam (3.2%),  Kalmunai (2.9%),  Anuradhapura  (2.6%),  Kurunegala  (2.5%),  and Badulla  (2%)  (see  Table  1)  (compared  to  the  previous week, colour of %: red=increase, green=decrease, blue=no change). WEEKLY DISTRIBUTION OF DENGUE PATIENTS in 2024, 2025 and 2026   Source: NaDSys – National Dengue Surveillance System HIGH RISK MOH AREAS  As presented in Table 2, during the 36th week of 2026, 35 Medical Officer of Health (MOH) areas were identified as high-risk, including 8 newly flagged areas (highlighted in light  red  in  Table  2).  Previously  classified  13  high-risk MOH areas in week 35, were not identified as high-risk in the 36th week of 2026 (Table 2). MIDNIGHT TOTAL OF DENGUE PATIENT ADMISSIONS * After incorporating delayed hospital reports, the average midnight total for the 35th week increased from 495 to 500. In  the  36th  week  of  2026,  the  average  midnight  total  of dengue  patients  across  73  sentinel  hospitals  was  449. Compared to the  previous  week, in the  36th  week,  21 hospitals reported an increase, while 30 reported a decrease.
